title: 6.15.9 Check: Sound and music
description: Eight multiple-choice questions on the browser's rule, loading once, play and loop, rate, a random pick, stopping the music on a new screen, and a saved 0. Checked instantly.

questions.question: A sketch calls `music.loop()` in `setup()`. In a fresh tab the tune stays silent until the player clicks the game, and then it starts. Why?
options: `loop()` always waits for a click on the canvas before it starts to play
The file only begins to download at the first click
`setup()` runs a second time on the first click
A browser lets a page make no sound before a click or a key
questions.explanation: Browsers refuse to make sound until the person has clicked or pressed a key on the page. moSHion switches sound on at the first one, and the loop that was waiting starts then.

questions.question: Why is `loadSound` called once in `setup()` and not in `draw()`?
options: `draw()` would start a new download every frame; a sound plays only once its file has arrived
`loadSound` stops the sketch with an error anywhere but `setup()`
A sound loaded in `draw()` plays sixty times a second, all on top of each other, until the game ends
Only `setup()` is allowed to give a variable its first value
questions.explanation: A file takes a moment to arrive, and play() before it has arrived does nothing. draw() runs 60 times a second, so loading there starts a fresh download every frame and none is ever ready.

questions.question: The code says `if (kb.pressing('3')) chime.play();` and the player holds 3 down for one second. What do they hear?
options: One chime, on the frame the key went down
One chime, on the frame the key came back up
About sixty chimes, one each frame, piled on top of each other
Nothing at all, because play() waits until the key has been let go again
questions.explanation: kb.pressing is true on every frame the key is held, and every play() starts a new copy. kb.presses is true only on the frame the key goes down: one press, one chime.

questions.question: `music.loop()` runs in `draw()`, every frame. What does the player hear?
options: Sixty copies of the tune a second, piling up
One copy of the tune, looping
The first moment of the tune, restarted every frame
Nothing, because `loop()` works only in `setup()`
questions.explanation: A sound has one looping copy. loop() while it is already looping does nothing, so calling it every frame is safe. play() is the one that starts a new copy every call.

questions.question: The thud is set up with `thud.rate = 0.5;` before `thud.play();`. Compared with a rate of 1, how does it sound?
options: The same note, only half as loud
Higher, and over in half the time
Lower, and twice as long
Exactly the same: rate only changes a looping sound
questions.explanation: rate is the playback speed, and the pitch moves with it. Half speed is lower and takes twice as long; 1.5 would be higher and shorter.

questions.question: `thuds` is a list of three sounds. Which line plays one of them, picked at random?
options: `thuds[random(3)].play();`
`thuds[thuds.length].play();`
`thuds[floor(random(thuds.length + 1))].play();`
`thuds[floor(random(thuds.length))].play();`
questions.explanation: thuds.length is 3, and floor(random(3)) is 0, 1 or 2: the three positions. random(3) alone gives a decimal such as 1.7, which is not a position; thuds.length + 1 can give 3, and thuds[3] is past the end.

questions.question: In `goTo(next)`, why does `music.stop()` come before the new screen's tune starts?
options: The old copy would carry on: `loop()` while looping does nothing, and `play()` adds a copy
`stop()` rewinds the file so the next start plays it from the beginning
The browser refuses to start a second sound while another sound from the same file is going
`stop()` downloads the file again, ready for the next screen
questions.explanation: Without stop(), the title loop would just keep going into the game (loop() while looping does nothing), and a win's play() would start on top of the game's loop.

questions.question: A player turned the level down to 0, and it was saved. Next time the game starts, `level = getItem('soundLevel') || 5;` runs. What is `level`?
options: 0, the level that was saved
5, because 0 counts as false for `||`, just like `null`
`null`, because a 0 is never saved
`'0'`, as text, because getItem always gives back a string of text
questions.explanation: getItem gives back the number 0, but || picks its right side whenever the left counts as false, and 0 does. if (saved !== null) level = saved; keeps the 0.
